logPresets.label: Nerve B-complex tablet (nicotinamide, enter label value)

warnings: Upper limit 35 mg per day from supplements and fortified foods (ICMR-NIN 2020, US NASEM); food niacin is not capped.
Nicotinic acid from about 30 mg can cause flushing, itching and dizziness; niacinamide does not cause flushing but long-term high doses should be checked with a doctor.

High-dose or sustained-release nicotinic acid can damage the liver and raise blood sugar and uric acid; avoid unless prescribed, especially with liver disease, diabetes, gout, peptic ulcer or alcohol use.
Niacin added to statins did not reduce heart attacks in large trials; do not self-treat cholesterol with niacin.
Check labels for duplicate B-complex products; many Indian capsules contain 100 mg niacinamide each.
A recurring dark scaly rash on sun-exposed skin with diarrhoea or confusion, especially with heavy drinking or TB treatment, needs medical care.
General information, not medical advice. Check with a doctor before starting supplements.
